column2: AI education North America 2026 adoption regulation players
column4: 134 AI-in-education bills across 31 states in 2026 (tracker count). California AB 1159 bars training AI models on student data; Idaho SB 1227 sets school-AI privacy requirements; Oklahoma and Maryland require human oversight and bar AI from high-stakes student decisions. Federal: K-12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 (H.R. 8747) advanced out of House Education and Workforce markup 2026-07-21 — ADVANCED, NOT LAW. District: NYC one-year moratorium on student-facing AI through grade 8; Katy ISD bans generative chatbots K-6; Columbia Law allows AI as a learning aid but not for submitted work. NA holds ~36% of the global AI-in-education market. 🔴 No comprehensive national AI law in force in ANY of the three NA economies; Canada's June 2026 "AI for All" strategy is literacy funding, not statute; Mexico has bills and no enforcing regulator

column2: AI education EMEA 2026 adoption regulation players
column3: 🟡 HELD on regulation, THIN on players
column4: EU AI Act is the binding frame and classifies admission decisions, student evaluation and exam scoring as HIGH-RISK, reaching non-EU vendors whose outputs affect EU-located students. 🔴 DATES CONFLICT ACROSS SOURCES in this leg (adoption 2024 with phasing through 2026-27; an AI Omnibus amendment in late July 2026; "high-risk provisions from Aug 2026") — carried as UNSETTLED, not asserted. European AI-in-education market ~$2.64B (2026, third-party estimate); Finland, Estonia and the Netherlands cited as K-12 integration leaders; UK £4M for lesson-planning/marking tools. ~10% of institutions have formal AI-use guidelines. 🔴 The leg named REGULATORS (European Commission, UNESCO, OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026) and NOT ONE EMEA ed-tech VENDOR. Declared as a gap

column2: AI education APAC 2026 adoption regulation players
column4: South Korea's Framework (Basic) Act on AI in force since 2026-01-22 — the region's broadest; generative-AI provisions require disclosure that the user is dealing with AI and marking of generated content. Vietnam's AI law in force 2026-03-01; a July 2026 decision lists EDUCATION among six high-risk sectors (automated assessment, behavioural monitoring), high-risk only where AI output is the SOLE basis for a decision without meaningful human review. 🔴 Compliance deadline for education DISPUTED between sources (Sept 2027 vs March 2027 + six-month grace for systems already operating) — carried as UNSETTLED. Taiwan: principles-based AI Basic Act, national AI committee from March 2026. Japan promotes without penalties; China regulates by service type; Singapore, India, Australia rely on voluntary guidance. Ipsos Education Monitor 2026: support for BANNING AI in schools ranges 23% (Indonesia) to 31% (South Korea). 🔴 South/Southeast Asia policy data thin; Indonesia's AI presidential regulations still pending mid-2026

column2: AI education LATAM 2026 adoption regulation players
column3: 🟢 HELD, the strongest primary source of the four
column4: UNESCO IESALC + UNU-IAS surveyed 200 institutions across 19 countries: 87% use AI in at least one area, only 26% have a formal AI strategy, 74% use it in teaching and learning, and adoption is driven by INDIVIDUAL academics and students rather than institutional strategy. UNESCO launched the Observatory on AI in Education for LAC on 2026-04-14 at ECLAC, Santiago. Digital Education Council LATAM survey: 30 000+ responses across 29 institutions. Uruguay first in the region to sign the Council of Europe AI framework convention (2025); Colombia CONPES 4144 (Feb 2025); Mexico's federal risk-based bill proposes an oversight authority; Peru's law adds regulatory sandboxes. Mexico UNESCO pilot with CONALEP and DGETI. 🔴 The leg found NO 2026 regulation SPECIFIC to AI in schools or universities — the LATAM picture is general AI law plus institutional governance. ILIA: school-level gains "remain exceptions"
